name: NC-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with +17 partisan lean
Incumbent Deborah Ross running with large financial advantage
Republican challenger has raised essentially nothing
model.rationale: The district's +17 Democratic lean, Ross's incumbency and roughly $1.7 million raised against an unfunded Republican challenger all point to a lopsided race, and markets price her win probability around 94%. The forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late outside spending or polling showing a tighter race would be the first sign of movement, but nothing currently suggests it.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Deborah Ross, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Raleigh-area district that leans heavily Democratic by about 17 points. She has raised roughly $1.7 million and holds over $1.3 million on hand, while Republican Eugene Douglass has reported no meaningful fundraising and no outside groups are active in the race. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public general-election polls cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the financial gap, and prediction markets, which price Ross's chances around 94 percent. Everything points to a comfortable Democratic hold.
